The Quran has 114 surahs, from Al-Fatihah to An-Nas.
Al-Fatihah is called Umm al-Kitab because it opens the Quran and gathers its core themes.
Al-Baqarah has 286 ayat, more than any other surah.
Al-Kawthar has only three short ayat, making it the shortest surah.
The Quran itself says it was sent down in the month of Ramadan (Al-Baqarah 2:185).
The first revelation came in the Cave of Hira, on Jabal an-Nur near Makkah.
The first words revealed were the opening of Surah Al-Alaq: “Read in the name of your Lord.”
At-Tawbah is the only surah that does not begin with Bismillah.
An-Naml opens with Bismillah and has it again inside the letter of Sulayman (27:30).
Ayat al-Kursi is verse 255 of Surah Al-Baqarah.
The Prophet ﷺ said Surah Al-Ikhlas equals a third of the Quran (Sahih al-Bukhari).
The Quran is divided into 30 ajza’, so many people read one juz’ a day in Ramadan.
The Hijrah in 622 CE marks the start of the Hijri calendar.
The Prophet ﷺ was born in Makkah.
He was born in the Year of the Elephant, when Abraha’s army marched on Makkah.
Badr, in 2 AH, was the first major battle between the Muslims and Quraysh.
The Battle of Badr took place in Ramadan, 2 AH.
At Al-Khandaq in 5 AH, the Muslims dug a trench to defend Madinah.
The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was agreed in 6 AH and brought a truce with Quraysh.
Maryam is the only woman named in the Quran, and a surah carries her name.
Five daily prayers are obligatory: Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha.
Surah Al-Isra opens with the Night Journey from Masjid al-Haram to Masjid al-Aqsa.
Hadith encourage reciting Surah Al-Kahf on Friday.
Al-Kahf tells of young believers who sheltered in a cave and slept for many years.
Surah Al-Qadr says Laylatul Qadr is better than a thousand months (97:3).
Masjid Quba, built on arrival near Madinah during the Hijrah, was the first masjid the Prophet ﷺ built.
The qiblah was changed from Jerusalem to the Ka’bah in 2 AH (Al-Baqarah 2:144).
The revelation came over about 23 years.
The angel Jibril brought the revelation to the Prophet ﷺ.
Al-Fatihah has seven ayat and is recited in every rak’ah of salah.
An-Nas is the 114th and final surah in the order of the Mushaf.
Musa is named more than any other prophet in the Quran, over 130 times.
Surah Yusuf (12:3) calls its account “the best of stories.”
An-Nahl means “The Bee,” and the surah mentions honey as a healing for people (16:69).
The first revelation came when the Prophet ﷺ was about 40 years old.
Madinah was called Yathrib before the Hijrah.
Surah Al-Jumu’ah calls believers to hurry to the Friday prayer (62:9).
Surah Al-Fil recalls how Allah protected the Ka’bah from Abraha’s army with elephants.
Ar-Rahman repeats “Which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?” 31 times.
Al-Baqarah is named after the story of the cow in ayat 67 to 73.
The five pillars are the shahadah, salah, zakah, fasting Ramadan and Hajj (Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim).
Belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day and qadar, from the hadith of Jibril (Sahih Muslim).
The rites of Hajj take place in the early days of Dhul-Hijjah, the last month of the Hijri year.
Zakah is due on savings above the nisab once they have been held for a full lunar year (the hawl).
Zakah on money and trade goods is one-fortieth, or 2.5%.
Maghrib is the only obligatory prayer with three rak'ahs.
Fajr 2, Dhuhr 4, Asr 4, Maghrib 3 and Isha 4 add up to 17.
Maghrib begins when the sun has set.
The Prophet ﷺ chose Bilal, known for his strong, beautiful voice, to call the adhan in Madinah.
Wudu, the ablution, washes the hands, mouth, nose, face, arms, head (wiped) and feet (Al-Ma'idah 5:6).
When water can't be used, the Quran allows tayammum with clean earth (An-Nisa' 4:43, Al-Ma'idah 5:6).
The Friday prayer, with its khutbah, is prayed at Dhuhr time in congregation.
Tarawih are the extra night prayers many masjids pray in congregation during Ramadan.
The Prophet ﷺ said, “Eat suhur, for in suhur there is blessing” (Sahih al-Bukhari).
Eid al-Fitr is on the 1st of Shawwal, right after Ramadan.
Eid al-Adha is the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah, the day after 'Arafah.
Pilgrims stand at 'Arafah on the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah, the heart of Hajj.
Zakat al-Fitr is paid before the Eid prayer so everyone can celebrate Eid.
The Prophet ﷺ used to do i'tikaf in the last ten days of Ramadan (Sahih al-Bukhari).
The Prophet ﷺ said to seek it in the odd nights of the last ten of Ramadan (Sahih al-Bukhari).
Hijri months follow the moon, so Ramadan lasts 29 or 30 days.
The Hijri year begins with Muharram.
The Quran says the number of months with Allah is twelve (At-Tawbah 9:36).
Ramadan is the ninth month, between Sha'ban and Shawwal.
Shawwal follows Ramadan, and Eid al-Fitr is its first day.
At-Tawbah 9:36 mentions four sacred months: Dhul-Qa'dah, Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram and Rajab.
Abu Bakr led the Muslims after the Prophet ﷺ passed away in 11 AH.
Under Uthman, standardized copies of the Mushaf were made and sent out to the Muslim cities.
Abu Bakr hid with him in the cave, “the second of the two” (At-Tawbah 9:40).
Young Ali stayed behind in his bed, then returned the trusts people had left with the Prophet ﷺ.
Khadijah bint Khuwaylid was his first wife and the first to believe in his message.
Umar was called al-Faruq, the one who distinguishes truth from falsehood.
The Prophet ﷺ gave Khalid ibn al-Walid the title Sword of Allah.
Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the Lion of Allah, was martyred at Uhud.
Abu Talib took him in at about age eight and protected him for years.
Abd al-Muttalib cared for him after his mother died.
Halimah of the Banu Sa'd nursed him in the desert.
Sumayyah, the mother of Ammar ibn Yasir, was killed in Makkah for refusing to give up her faith.
After the first Pledge of 'Aqabah, Mus'ab ibn Umayr went to teach the Quran in Yathrib.
Salman al-Farisi suggested the trench, a Persian defense the Arabs had not used before.
Abu Hurayrah narrated more hadith than any other companion.
The people of Makkah called him al-Amin. Amanah, trust, comes from the same root as our masjid's name.
The Battle of Uhud took place in 3 AH beside Mount Uhud.
Makkah was opened in Ramadan of 8 AH, with a general amnesty.
Hunayn was fought in 8 AH, just after the opening of Makkah.
The expedition to Tabuk was in 9 AH.
The Farewell Hajj was in 10 AH, a few months before he passed away.
About 13 years in Makkah, then about 10 in Madinah.
He lived in Madinah for about ten years, from 1 AH to 11 AH.
He passed away in Madinah in 11 AH at the age of 63.
He is buried in Madinah, in what was 'Aishah's room, now within Masjid an-Nabawi.
In about the fifth year of prophethood, a group migrated to Abyssinia (Habashah).
An-Najashi (the Negus) gave the Muslim refugees his protection.
Ja'far explained Islam and recited from Surah Maryam, and the king refused to hand them over.
In Ta'if he was rejected and stoned, yet he made du'a for their descendants to believe.
People of Yathrib pledged at 'Aqabah, which opened the way to the Hijrah.
He paired emigrants and helpers as brothers, and many Ansar shared their homes and wealth.
The five daily prayers were made obligatory on the night of the Mi'raj (Sahih al-Bukhari).
Masjid an-Nabawi, the Prophet's Masjid, was built soon after the Hijrah.
After Masjid al-Haram and Masjid an-Nabawi, Masjid al-Aqsa in Jerusalem is the third.
The khatib stands on the minbar. A carved minbar is one of our masjid projects.
The minaret lets the adhan carry across the neighborhood.
The well of Zamzam sprang up for Hajar and baby Isma'il.
Ibrahim and Isma'il raised its foundations (Al-Baqarah 2:127).
Pilgrims walk between Safa and Marwah seven times in the sa'y.
Pilgrims enter ihram before reaching Makkah.
The black kiswah, embroidered in gold, is replaced every year.
Yunus called on Allah from the belly of the fish and was saved (As-Saffat 37:139-148).
Nuh built the Ark by Allah's command (Hud 11:37).
“O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim” (Al-Anbiya' 21:69).
Ayyub stayed patient and Allah restored him (Sad 38:41-44).
Sulayman heard the ant warn the others and smiled (An-Naml 27:16-19).
“And to Dawud We gave the Zabur” (An-Nisa' 4:163).
The Tawrah was revealed to Musa.
Salih was sent to Thamud, and the she-camel was their sign (Al-A'raf 7:73).
Shu'ayb told Madyan to give full measure and weight (Al-A'raf 7:85).
Adam, the first human, was also the first prophet.
Twenty-five prophets are named in the Quran.
“And Allah took Ibrahim as a close friend” (An-Nisa' 4:125).
Musa asked for his brother Harun to support him (Ta-Ha 20:29-32). A good teammate.
Yusuf explained the dream, and Egypt prepared for the famine (Yusuf 12:43-49).
Musa's staff became a snake before Pharaoh (Ta-Ha 20:19-21).
“And We made iron soft for him” (Saba' 34:10).
'Isa was born to Maryam without a father (Aal-'Imran 3:47).
Allah gave Zakariyya the good news of a son named Yahya in his old age (Maryam 19:7).
He is the Messenger of Allah and the seal of the prophets (Al-Ahzab 33:40).
“And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds” (Al-Anbiya' 21:107).
“And indeed, you are of a great moral character” (Al-Qalam 68:4).
The Prophet ﷺ called Al-Baqarah and Aal-'Imran the two bright ones (Sahih Muslim).
The two surahs of seeking refuge, often recited for protection.
It is named after the table sent down, asked for by the disciples of 'Isa (5:112-115).
It compares false protectors to a spider's house, the weakest of houses (29:41).
It tells of the ant who warned the others as Sulayman's army came (27:18).
Al-Hadid means iron, which the surah mentions as having great strength (57:25).
It opens: “Nun. By the pen and what they write” (68:1).
“By time, indeed mankind is in loss”, except those who believe, do good and advise each other to truth and patience (103).
Surah Quraysh (106) reminds them of the trade journeys Allah made safe for them.
Luqman advises his son on tawhid, salah, patience and humility (31:13-19).
Dhul-Qarnayn's journeys and the wall he built are in Al-Kahf (18:83-98).
“Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth” (An-Nur 24:35).
At-Tin (95) begins “By the fig and the olive.”
Al-'Adiyat means the charging (horses) that run panting (100:1).
Al-Ma'un (107) connects faith with caring for the orphan and the poor.
Surah 111 is known as both Al-Masad and Al-Lahab.
Al-Baqarah 2:282, about writing down debts, is the longest ayah.
We say bismillah before we start something, even a game.
Subhanallah declares Allah free of every imperfection.
Alhamdulillah, the first words after the basmalah in Al-Fatihah.
The Quran teaches us to say in sha Allah about the future (Al-Kahf 18:23-24).
Masha'Allah praises Allah for the good you see (Al-Kahf 18:39).
The Prophet ﷺ sought Allah's forgiveness more than seventy times a day (Sahih al-Bukhari).
The Quran says to return a greeting with a better one or at least the same (An-Nisa' 4:86).
The Prophet ﷺ taught this as an excellent way to thank someone (Sunan at-Tirmidhi).
Islam means submitting to Allah, and it shares a root with salam, peace.
Quran comes from qara'a, to read or recite.
The Sunnah is what he said, did and approved.
Tafsir explains the meanings of the Quran.
Tajwid covers pronunciation, lengthening and pauses.
A hafiz (or hafizah) carries the whole Quran in memory. That's where the Hikmah meter comes from on the court.
Sadaqah can be anything good, even a smile (Sunan at-Tirmidhi).
Come back after your next game.
The bookshelf opens after your first career game.
You have studied every book on the shelf, masha’Allah.
Welcome to my office. Come see the bookshelf after your first game, and ask me anything.
Sit, sit. My door is open after every game. Bring questions, not only complaints.
Good win, alhamdulillah. The real test is how you carry it.
Remember the brothers who rebounded and set screens. Nobody scores alone.
A win is a blessing to be thankful for, not a reason to feel bigger than anyone.
You played with composure today. That’s worth more than the points.
Say alhamdulillah, then go thank whoever set your screens.
Winning with good manners is winning twice.
A loss isn’t the end of the story. Sabr, then back to the gym.
We learn more from losses than wins, if we’re honest with ourselves.
Allah doesn’t burden a soul beyond what it can bear (2:286). You can carry this one.
Losses show us what to practice. That’s a gift, even if it doesn’t feel like one.
Did you give your best effort? Then the result is with Allah. The effort is what you control.
Shake it off, pray, sleep. Tomorrow we fix the details.
A trophy, alhamdulillah. Share the credit and keep the intention you started with.
Champions. Put the trophy on the shelf, and put the humility in your heart.
The Quran says if you are grateful, Allah will give you more (14:7). So let’s be grateful.
Enjoy this. Then remember that the next stage starts at zero, for everyone.
Three wins in a row, masha’Allah. Stay humble. Streaks end, character stays.
You’re rolling. Keep praying on time and keep passing the ball. Don’t change what works.

Masjid Al-Amanah, Eastside. Your first week in town, your first Isha here.
Brother, I don’t know your face yet. Welcome. You’re new in Eastside?
Wa alaykum as-salam. I moved here last week.
Then you found the right door. The young ones play ball in the gym after Isha. Through there, past the shoe racks.
Wa iyyak. Go on. Tell Saleem the imam sent you.
Ha! The old man still has it.
Good effort. Get a drink, catch your breath, and we run it back.
Dad, don’t celebrate yet. One more.
Okay, okay. You can play. Where did you learn that move?
Good hands. Good feet. You box out, too. Nobody here boxes out.
Come back tomorrow. Same time. We need a fourth who doesn’t complain.
He’s right. And you passed when you were open, and passed when I was more open. That’s rare.
You let them score on you twice, Dad.
I let them? You missed four layups. Four!
Three. The fourth one was blocked. That’s not missing.
Yalla, it’s still a miss. A miss is a miss.
We lost a pickup game. We didn’t lose anything else. Come, let’s stack the chairs.
In sha Allah, I’ll be here tomorrow.
In sha Allah. Welcome to Al-Amanah, akhi.
The next night. After Isha the gym is full: uncles on folding chairs, kids at the far hoop, a dozen brothers you haven’t met.
You came back! Alhamdulillah. Ammo Jamil owes me five dollars.
I said he’d come back. I bet he’d be late.
Tonight, meet everyone. The gym first, then the musalla through the partition.
When you’ve said salaam to all of them, come and find me in my office. We have something to talk about.
Sit, sit. Let me tell you something about this gym.
Nineteen years I play here. Nineteen years we never win the masjid league. Not once.
Once we reached the final. Al-Furqan beat us by one. ONE point. I still see that shot when I close my eyes.
This year we win it. I am not getting any younger, and my knees are getting much older.
Don’t let my dad scare you. He’s been talking about that final since before I was born.
He wants the trophy. I just want him to watch me play one game without yelling “BEND YOUR KNEES.”
If we win, maybe he finally says “good game, son.” Two words. Three. You get it.
EVERYBODY UP! Lightning, five of us, loser stacks the chairs!
Five of us, two balls. You know the rules?
Make it before the man behind you does.
Bro. You knocked out Ilyas AND his dad in one game.
I let him. Respect for the guest.
You did not let him, Dad.
Got you! Welcome to Al-Amanah, we play for keeps.
Good effort. Now, chairs. Then my office.
Come in, close the door. The chai is from Imam Dawud, so it’s strong.
I never introduced myself properly. Saleem. I studied in Madinah, came back, and the masjid asked me to stay a year. That was eleven years ago.
Al-Amanah is small. Two hundred families, a gym that is also the overflow musalla, a weekend school in two rooms.
But the people here look after each other. Ammo Jamil drives the uncles to the doctor. Ustath Karim teaches for free. Musa found us at a park.
Everyone has been kind to me. In two days it already feels like home.
Alhamdulillah. That’s what a masjid is for.
Now. The league starts soon, and we play two on two. We have seven brothers for two spots on the floor at a time.
I saw your game. I want you on the team. But a starting spot is earned here, not given.
Tomorrow, outside, King of the Court. Hold the court and the spot is yours.
One on one, first to three. Hold the court three straight and you’re king.
Nobody holds the court on me. Nobody.
Can I dunk on him? Is that allowed?
Dad, you said that last time.
Not this time. Catch your breath, drink some water, and go again.
The court doesn’t give, it takes. Again!
Brothers, gather round. I think you all saw what I saw.
He boxes out. He passes. He doesn’t complain. I vote yes.
He shoots with his elbow in. I vote yes.
He said salaam to the uncles before the ball. Yes.
Two new guys on the team? We should get matching headbands.
We are not getting matching headbands.
Then it’s settled. Welcome to the Al-Amanah team, akhi. You’re here to help us win the masjid league.
May Allah put barakah in it. And may the chai never run out.
Salaam! You play? Good. Dad says I shoot too much.
Wa alaykum as-salam. Is there such a thing?
That’s what I keep telling him!
Ilyas! Bend your knees! …Oh. Wa alaykum as-salam. You’re new.
I just moved here. The imam sent me.
Ammo Jamil. That one shooting is my son. He thinks defense is optional.
Say salaam to the brothers first, then come see me.
Assalamu alaykum. I saw you at Isha. I’m Saleem.
Wa alaykum as-salam. The imam said to find you. Can I join in?
Of course. Warm up first. Shoot around, get a feel for the floor.
There he is. Go say salaam, brother.
Take your time. Finish your warm-up first.
Good. You’ve got a feel for it.
Two on two. You and me against Ammo Jamil and Ilyas. First to 11.
Finally. My knees are getting cold.

Shoot around. Move, sprint, get some shots up. Make a couple, then come find me.
Go on, meet everybody. Then we talk trophies.
The cones are by the far hoop. Try the cone run, Q opens the drills.
Ah, the brother from Isha. Come, have some chai.
Cardamom and patience. I make it after every Isha. Players drink first, then the uncles complain.
Salaam, beta! Don’t mind me. I’m just here for the chai and the shouting.

Meet everyone, try the gym out. When you’re done here, the musalla is through the partition.
Everyone in the gym met. Through the partition to the musalla.
As-salamu alaykum! You’re the new brother. I’m Anas. They call me Qari because I lead Taraweeh.
I also play center. Tall people don’t get a choice here.
Wa alaykum as-salam. I am Abdullah, the masjid’s mufti. People bring me their questions.
Mostly about inheritance. Sometimes whether the shot clock is halal. It is.
Zubair. I memorised the Quran when I was twelve, and I’ve kept score for the brothers ever since.
If there’s an argument about the score, they ask me. Nobody argues with a hafiz.
Ustath Karim. I teach the weekend school: forty-three kids in two rooms. And I shoot.
Sometimes it goes in. Mostly it goes in.
Yo! The other new guy! I’m Musa. I took my shahadah in the spring.
Everybody here taught me how to pray. Now I teach them how to dunk.
Practice with intention, akhi. Even ten free throws count.
You again! Good. Rebound for me.
One more round of shots? I’ll beat you this time.
Come in, all of you. Squeeze in. Musa, sit on the bookshelf if you have to.
Before the league starts, I want you to know why we play. It isn’t for a trophy.
Forty-three kids come to the weekend school. We teach them in two rooms. One of the rooms is the coat closet.
Last month we turned eleven families away. No space. Their kids go nowhere on the weekend.
The board approved a school wing on the parking lot side. Four classrooms. It costs one hundred thousand dollars.
One hundred thousand? We can barely pay for the electricity.
Every game we win, people come to watch. People who watch, give. The Masjid League final is the biggest night of our year.
The Prophet ﷺ said: when a person dies, his deeds end except three. One of them is knowledge that benefits.
Those classrooms will teach long after all of us are gone.
So every win builds a classroom.
Every win builds a little of one. And every bit of adab we show on the court brings the community with us.
The school wing fundraiser has begun. Its meter is on the hub.
Alhamdulillah. One down. Thank Allah, then thank the brother who set your screens.
A loss in the group stage is not the end. Win the next one and we’re still alive.
I hate losing. I REALLY hate losing.
Two wins. My weekend class made a poster. It is mostly glitter.
Keep the intention, keep the effort. One more group game.
We lost, and we lost with adab. Now we learn from it.
Practice, the next night. Halfway through a drill, the old tubes buzz… and go out. The whole gym goes dark.
Bro. BRO. I can’t see my own hands.
The breaker again. Nineteen years, same breaker.
Nobody move to the switch, the uncles are on it. In the meantime… two on two. In the dark.
How do we see the ball?
Listen for it. And watch the glow. Bismillah!
The lights flicker back to life.
That was the best game of my life and I didn’t see any of it.
You found your teammate without looking. That’s trust.
In the dark, the old man is king! Ha!
Win or lose, that was fun. Now: the breaker. Somebody call the electrician.
Alhamdulillah. Now we see where the table stands.
Sabr. Let’s see where the table stands.
We didn’t get out of the group. Third on the table.
We learn, we practice, and we come back. The league comes round again.
Through to the playoffs! Top two in the group, alhamdulillah.
A semifinal. One game to the final.
Single elimination now. Lose and go home.
Then we don’t think about losing. We think about the next possession.
The final. Twenty years ago I was in a final. Twenty years.
This time, Dad, we win it.
One game from the final. That stings.

Come, a glass of chai. The good glass. I keep it for the special ones.
Bro. Bro. We’re like… the best duo in the masjid.
When I took my shahadah, I was scared nobody would know me. Now look. I have you.
A ten. Masha’Allah. Do you know how much work that takes?
I do. I watched you in the gym when everyone else had gone home.
Seven or better in everything. You can do whatever the team needs now.
That’s what a masjid needs too: people who can carry any part of it.
Fifty games, akhi! I counted. Well, Ustath Karim counted. I helped.
Next fifty, I want to win HORSE against you at least once.
Five times. Five! My uncle is furious. He’s also asked me to ask you to come to dinner.
Al-Furqan and Al-Amanah. Same street, same Lord. See you on the court, brother.
FIVE DUNKS. In one game! The crowd was SHAKING.
Teach me. Please. Fundamentals first, I know, I know. Then dunks.
You won CHAI. So someone else made the chai.
It was terrible. Thank you. I have not laughed like that in years.
Lights out, CHAI, the all-star game, the draw in Istanbul. You did all of it.
Some people only remember the trophies. I remember the nights in between.
One hundred and fifty thousand. The wing is built, so the board has a new idea: scholarships.
Every child at the weekend school, whatever their family can pay. Because of the games you played.
Champions again. You don’t need the story to have a reason to play.
This is what it was always about: brothers, a ball, a masjid, and Allah’s blessing on all of it.
Every milestone. Late one night after Isha, the brothers are all still in the gym.
Akhi. Come here. Everyone wanted to be here for this.
We have something for you. Imam Dawud, the box.
A basketball. Painted gold. The kids did it at the weekend school. It took them three Saturdays.
It goes on a stand in the gym. Where everyone can see it.
One day a new brother will walk in here, nervous, not knowing anyone. And he will see it and ask about it.
And we will tell him about you.
And then we will make him play HORSE.
The Prophet ﷺ said: the most beloved of people to Allah are those most beneficial to people. You were that for us.
The golden ball now sits on its stand in the gym. Walk up to it any time.

texts: Your story at Masjid Al-Amanah: the league, the masjid, the brothers.
A two-minute tutorial teaches moving, shooting, layups, dunks,
passing and defense. You can always find it in Quick Play.

steps.how: do the previous lesson (it moves on by itself)

steps.title: Tutorial lesson 5: Pass
steps.how: do the previous lesson (it moves on by itself)
texts: Drive in and press H toward the rim: a layup, released for you.
K near the rim: a dunk or a floater.

steps.title: Tutorial lesson 6: Dribble moves
steps.how: do the previous lesson (it moves on by itself)
texts: Tap J to pass to your partner. The pass type picks itself.

steps.title: Tutorial lesson 7: Defend
steps.how: do the previous lesson (it moves on by itself)
texts: Press H while pushing a direction: crossover, spin or
step-back. Double-tap H for your signature move.

steps.title: Tutorial lesson 8: Steal
steps.how: do the previous lesson (it moves on by itself)
texts: Hold H (or L) on defense: you guard your man, staying
between him and the rim. Stay with him.
